editor_comparator.why_unusable: every net row carries an empty PCB pin list, including the nets whose pins match exactly, while the same PCB exports a 165556-character netlist with 62 named nets and 254 assigned pins

interpretation: Every pin present on both sides pairs by (designator, pin number); no PCB pin is missing a schematic partner.
The only unmatched pins are the 24 logical terminals of CT and T1-T4, whose PCB pads are design-owned placeholders with no designator, so they are not component pins in the PCB netlist.
PRI_12, PRI_23 and PRI_34 exist only in the schematic because every pin on them is a magnetic terminal.
The five D_CT1-D_CT4 and U2 pin-2 pads carry no net on either side; they are the same unassigned pins on both sides, not a difference.

The single native Netlist Error is consistent with these five magnetics having no PCB component, and no other pin-level difference exists in the editor's own export; the DRC rule reports a count, not items, so mapping that count to these rows remains an inference.
limitations: The comparator's PCB column is unusable on this primitive-built board; the difference above comes from the PCB's own netlist export, not from it.
Anonymous pads can carry a net name while remaining outside any component pin list; that is a placeholder fact, not a verified physical terminal map.
Pin pairing by (designator, pin number) does not prove footprint geometry, polarity, insulation or assembly.
